An anti-inflammatory drug, interleukin-6 antibody, failed in a clinical trial of participants with heart disease and high CRP, IL-6 levels. That doesn't detract from the body of evidence incriminating inflammation as a root cause of cardiovascular events, and the success of other anti-inflammatory drugs to prevent heart attacks (interleukin-1β, colchicine). 
Moreover, coronary artery inflammation was not measured, and it can be now.
